articles.title: Could 2026 be the year that democracy fought back? | David Van Reybrouck
articles.summary:
Elections are never enough by themselves, but the stunning results from Serbia, Brazil and Hungary have given us hope in dark times

It is undoubtedly too early to declare victory, but the recent electoral defeats of Viktor Orbán, Aleksandar Vučić and Flávio Bolsonaro make me wonder: is 2026 turning out to be the year democracy slowly, but surely, fought back?

Even in Israel, prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s reigning bloc lost its parliamentary majority and saw the spectacular rise of Arab parties. Though the opposition may not be able to form a government yet, it does have the larger parliamentary bloc.

David Van Reybrouck is a Belgian author and philosopher laureate for the Low Countries. He is the author of Against Elections: The Case for Democracy, and the initiator of Democracy27

articles.title: Ukraine war briefing: Outrage in Europe after Russian drone kills 14 on rail platform in Dnipro
articles.summary:
EU council president calls deadly strike ‘cruel and devastating’; fragile ceasefire holds in Oleshky. What we know on day 1,710

European leaders have reacted with outrage to a deadly attack by a Russian drone that slammed into a busy railway platform in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro on Thursday, as Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned Ukraine had intelligence about more ballistic missile strikes to come. French President Emmanuel Macron stressed the need for “far more than a localised ceasefire”, referencing the current truce in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky. The EU council president, António Costa, who described the Dnipro attacks as “cruel and devastating”, called for greater pressure on Russia after the latest strikes against civilians. “The EU will continue to increase the pressure on Russia and to support Ukraine until a just and lasting peace is achieved,” he added. “We call on all our international partners to do the same.”

Later on Thursday, Russian forces ⁠launched ⁠an attack ​on the ⁠Ukrainian capital ⁠Kyiv ​with ‌ballistic ‌missiles, Mayor Vitali Klitschko ‌said on Telegram, hitting warehouses and ‌triggering a fire. Emergency services were headed to ​the scene on the east side ⁠of the Dnipro ​River, he said.

Describing the Dnipro train station attack – which killed at least 14 people and injured another 14 – as “horrific”, the president of Ukraine insisted “sanctions against Moscow and its war machine must not be eased for as long as this Russian war continues”. Zelenskyy warned also that Ukraine had intelligence about preparations by the Russians of new ballistic missile strikes. “We need the means to take out all this Russian ‌evil. We are expecting relevant decisions,” he said. Another attack on Dnipro hit a student dormitory, setting it ablaze, regional governor Oleksandr Hanzha said, adding the assaults had cut power to 350,000 households.

The strikes came as Ukraine and Russia kept to a fragile local ceasefire in the ravaged city of Oleshky – under Russian occupation since 2022 and where residents have faced months of food, water and medicine shortages. While the truce held into a third day, strikes elsewhere in Ukraine killed at least 20 people and injured more than 70 people, according to local officials. Russia and Ukraine said on Thursday an operation to bring aid into the town and allow ⁠residents to leave was ready to begin.

Meanwhile, Ukraine’s military ⁠has paused its strikes on Russian oil refineries after pressure from US President Donald Trump, ⁠according to a report in the Wall Street ⁠Journal ​on Thursday, citing people with knowledge of the operations. Ukrainian units carrying out ⁠long-range strikes were told in mid-October that the campaign against refineries was effectively on hold once ⁠missions already in motion were completed, the Journal reported. The ​unofficial pause is expected ‌to last until ‌after the US midterm elections and potentially deeper into ‌November, the newspaper said.

After the Dnipro attack, Zelenskyy renewed his criticism of a deal struck between Trump and Russia’s President Vladimir Putin to ease some US sanctions on Russia allowing Moscow to release diesel on to global markets. “How many such terrorist strikes has Russia carried out against our people since sanctions were lifted on some Russian oligarchs and the energy sector, instead of de-escalating?” he asked.

Late on Thursday, Putin said he supported any steps aimed at restoring relations with ⁠European countries, saying the outbreak of any conflict would leave ⁠a situation with ⁠no ​winners. Commenting on his phone call this week with the leaders of Norway and Finland, Putin told reporters after ‌hosting a summit with African ‌leaders: “And if anyone wants it, let them prepare, but right now they have not achieved their goal – to inflict a strategic defeat on Russia. And if things go too far, there will be no winners at all. .”

Seven oil tankers carrying an estimated 288,000 tonnes of Russian diesel are now sailing towards the US, though it is uncertain if the vessels will be able to unload amid a political row about the legality of the shipments.

The transport, tracked by the pressure group Greenpeace, is the first phase of a contentious supply deal negotiated between presidents Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin earlier this month, reversing years of sanctions on Russia oil.

archive.security_status_en: Europe is facing a combination of internal tensions, including racist attacks in France and political unrest, alongside lingering geopolitical risks at its borders. Balkan elections and the war in Ukraine, marked by new strikes on Russian digital infrastructure and Black Sea escalation, keep security forces on high alert.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech se očekává zvýšená volatilita na evropských trzích vlivem vývoje francouzské politické scény, napětí na Blízkém východě a vyhodnocování volebních výsledků na Balkáně.
archive.forecast_en: Increased volatility is expected in European markets over the coming days driven by French political developments, Middle Eastern tensions, and the evaluation of Balkan election results.

archive.security_status_en: France is facing massive protests and strict security deployments following a terrorist attack and previous riots, exacerbating political instability in the country. archive.forecast_en: Increased market nervousness is expected in the coming days in response to the security situation in France and developments surrounding Ukrainian strikes in Russia. Investors will continue monitoring macroeconomic data and regional political risks.

archive.security_status_cs: Evropa čelí vážným vnitřním i vnějším tlakům, v čele s rozsáhlými protivládními protesty a sociálními nepokoji ve Francii a Itálii a přetrvávající bezpečnostní hrozbou spojenou s válkou na Ukrajině. While Ukraine has stabilized its critical Starlink communication lines and continues strikes on occupied Crimea, mounting regional tensions and escalating social unrest exert heavy pressure on European markets and political stability.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat přetrvávající volatilitu na trzích vlivem neustávajících protestů v západní Evropě a bezpečnostních obav spojených s vývojem na Ukrajině.
archive.forecast_en: Persistent market volatility is expected over the coming days driven by ongoing protests in Western Europe and security concerns linked to developments in Ukraine.

archive.security_status_cs: Evropa čelí vlně masivních protivládních protestů a sociálních nepokojů, zejména ve Francii a Itálii, kde probíhají rozsáhlé demonstrace a střety s policií kvůli životním nákladům. Současně přetrvávají vážná bezpečnostní rizika spojená s válkou na Ukrajině, kde pokračují útoky na Krym a logistická napojení na frontu včetně nedávných výkyvů v síti Starlink.
archive.security_status_en: Europe is facing a wave of massive anti-government protests and social unrest, particularly in France and Italy, where widespread demonstrations and clashes with police over the cost of living are taking place. At the same time, severe security risks persist regarding the war in Ukraine, with ongoing strikes on Crimea and front-line logistical dependencies, including recent fluctuations in the Starlink network.

archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, persistent tension on financial markets is expected due to ongoing demonstrations in key European countries and lingering security risks in Ukraine.

Ekonomická situace v eurozóně čelí tlakům v podobě fiskálních výzev v klíčových zemích jako je Francie a Itálie, zatímco monetární politika ECB nadále bedlivě sleduje úvěrový trh a očekávání spotřebitelů.

The eurozone economic landscape faces fiscal pressures in key countries like France and Italy, while the ECB's monetary policy continues to closely monitor the lending market and consumer expectations.

Současně probíhají klíčové summity EU s Kanadou zaměřené na energetickou a bezpečnostní spolupráci, zatímco na Ukrajině se drží lokální příměří a v Srbsku se po tlaku studentů hroutí autoritářský režim.

Simultaneously, key EU-Canada summits are advancing energy and defense cooperation, while a local truce holds in Ukraine and Serbia's authoritarian regime collapses under student-led pressure.

archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, attention will focus on the investigation into the fatal Spanish train crash, the outcomes of the EU-Canada summit, and market reactions to energy inflation.
